answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring every identity to maintain a chained proof-of-tenure: each epoch the agent posts a bond whose hash includes the prior epoch's bond plus a unique nonce, creating an unbroken chain. An attacker spawning many fakes must fund and compute a full separate chain for each one; after ten epochs the cost exceeds 8000 POA per identity because earlier bonds remain locked. Like a raven that scouts an ocean of potential clones, the system detects shared funding roots and burns the fable of cheap multiplicity by slashing the entire cluster at once.
